ethics_check.title: Ethics Approval Check
ethics_check.summary_text: All papers that appeared to involve live data collection contained an ethics approval statement.

table.text: The ethics committee of Isfahan University of Medical Sciences approved the study protocol (IR.MUI.MED.REC.1402.164), and the trial was registered at the Iran Registry of Clinical Trials (IRCT20230827059280N1).
The study was conducted in accordance with the principles of the Declaration of Helsinki.
All participants provided written informed consent.

Participants were withdrawn from the study under the following situations: poor treatment compliance (e.g., failure to take the prescribed medication as instructed), failure to return for scheduled follow-up visits, voluntary withdrawal from the study, development of severe side effects such as anaphylaxis, or requirement for further treatment with probiotics, antibiotics, or PPIs after completion of the study regimen.

Participants were allocated to the three study groups using a computer-generated block randomization sequence (block size of six, allocation ratio 1:1:1) generated using Random Allocation software by an investigator not involved in participant recruitment, treatment administration, or outcome assessment.
Participants were classified as adherent only if empty containers for all prescribed medications were returned, confirming completion of the full course.
Nonadherent participants were excluded from the per-protocol analysis.
Participants were also permitted to return for evaluation in case of serious adverse events, such as hypersensitivity reactions, at any point during the study period.
For the ITT analysis, all randomized participants were included.

Among the participants enrolled in the parent three-arm trial, 218 were randomized to the placebo group (n = 109) or the S. boulardii group (n = 109), which constitute the treatment arms analyzed in the present study.
As a result, 198 participants (98 and 100, respectively) were included in the per-protocol analysis, whereas all 218 randomized participants were included in the intention-to-treat (ITT) analysis.

power.title: Power Analysis Check

table.text: Sample size was calculated separately for the planned pairwise comparisons of S. boulardii versus placebo and rosuvastatin versus placebo in the parent three-arm trial. Because both experimental comparisons shared a common placebo comparator, we estimated the expected eradication rate in the placebo group from a previous randomized trial in which patients received the same bismuthcontaining quadruple therapy regimen (P-BAC) plus placebo. 25 An absolute difference of 20% in eradication rate (85.45% vs. 65.45%) was considered the minimum clinically meaningful treatment effect, given the local healthcare setting, treatment costs, the high prevalence of antibiotic resistance, and the potential adverse events of adjunctive therapies. Using a two-sided α level of 0.05 and 90% power, the required sample size was calculated with the formula for comparing two independent proportions. The calculated sample size was subsequently increased by 10% to account for anticipated participant attrition, resulting in a target enrollment of 109 participants per group. This sample size was applied uniformly across all three study arms.

In this setting with high resistance and high prevalence, adjunctive S. boulardii did not significantly improve H. pylori eradication when added to 14-day P-BAC therapy. Our study was designed to detect a prespecified 20-percentage-point difference but may have had limited power to detect smaller effects. S. boulardii significantly reduced treatment-related adverse events, particularly bloating and epigastric pain. live_data_statements: All participants provided written informed consent.

Participants were withdrawn from the study under the following situations: poor treatment compliance (e.g., failure to take the prescribed medication as instructed), failure to return for scheduled follow-up visits, voluntary withdrawal from the study, development of severe side effects such as anaphylaxis, or requirement for further treatment with probiotics, antibiotics, or PPIs after completion of the study regimen.

Participants were allocated to the three study groups using a computer-generated block randomization sequence (block size of six, allocation ratio 1:1:1) generated using Random Allocation software by an investigator not involved in participant recruitment, treatment administration, or outcome assessment.
Participants were classified as adherent only if empty containers for all prescribed medications were returned, confirming completion of the full course.
Nonadherent participants were excluded from the per-protocol analysis.
Participants were also permitted to return for evaluation in case of serious adverse events, such as hypersensitivity reactions, at any point during the study period.
For the ITT analysis, all randomized participants were included.

Among the participants enrolled in the parent three-arm trial, 218 were randomized to the placebo group (n = 109) or the S. boulardii group (n = 109), which constitute the treatment arms analyzed in the present study.
As a result, 198 participants (98 and 100, respectively) were included in the per-protocol analysis, whereas all 218 randomized participants were included in the intention-to-treat (ITT) analysis.
